title: Install playbook experiments + weird DNS cases — March 2027
content:
Purpose: capture the week’s standups, notes from on-call handover, and the low-effort experiments we ran on the install playbook to reduce DNS flakiness for VPC/on-prem installs. This is a working doc — notes, tests, and open questions below.

Quick summary:
- Field installs: 3 in-region VPC installs, 1 on-prem appliance (EU customer) — all completed but one had lingering DNS resolution flakiness causing healthcheck churn.
- Root cause hypothesis: intermittent split-brain between customer DNS cache and our installation bootstrap script; TTLs + small race window during node bootstrap cause ephemeral host lookup failures for 30–90s.
- Experiments run: added exponential backoff + DNS cache flush step in playbook; staged a small handshake (mTLS probe) before service start to avoid relying on external A records transiently.
- Result: reduced observed healthcheck failures from ~4 per install down to 0–1 for the last two installs.

Standup notes (raw):
- Mon AM handoff (Ravi -> Liam): observed install-007 (EU corp-edge) failing noderunner ready checks. Logs show "lookup: temporary failure" for internal.registry.redwood.example during init phase. Customer uses local DNS forwarder that has stale A record to a decommissioned NAT cluster.
- Action: postponed service start, triggered nsclean (cache flush) and then re-ran bootstrap. Service came up.
- Tue pairing (Liam + Gina): instrumented playbook to call 'resolvectl flush-caches' (systemd-resolved hosts) where available, and to run 'getent hosts' loop until expected A record resolves consistently 3x in a 15s window (empirical threshold).
- Wed: ran a canary by staging playbook change via PR-342 to a dev VPC cluster in NYC. Observed that init time increased by ~12s but flakiness dropped.
- Thu: on-prem install (customer ID: AURORA-21) had custom DNS setup (embedded appliance) and a DNS server that responds to UDP queries but drops large packets — caused truncated responses and the resolver falling back to TCP which was blocked by a micro ACL. We documented a workaround: open TCP 53 in the install window, and added a playbook check to detect truncated responses.

Incidents / customer blockers (detailed):
- Incident: EU-corp-edge (install-007)
  - Symptom: repeated healthcheck failures for control-plane -> registry during first 3 minutes after container runtime start.
  - Evidence: init logs (attached to JIRA-PLAT-1198) with repeated "Name or service not known" and then later "temporary failure in name resolution".
  - Team triage: network + infra + field-eng synced; quick repro on staging shown, mitigation applied (cache flush + pause).
  - Short-term mitigation: manual run of cache flush + restart. Customer asked for automated fix in playbook.
  - Long-term asks: add passive DNS monitoring on the bootstrap path and a ticket to customer success to get their DNS team to confirm no stale entries.

- Incident: On-prem appliance (AURORA-21)
  - Symptom: installer hung on curl to control-plane endpoint; tcpdump showed multiple TCP retransmits after UDP truncation.
  - Root cause: old NAT box performing DNS manipulation (EDNS0 truncation) + firewall blocking fallback TCP.
  - Mitigation: allowed TCP/53 for install window; installer resumed.
  - Follow-up: create an adapted pre-install checklist for appliances with older DNS stacks; include a simple remote-check script we can share with field team.

Playbook experiments & changes (what we tried):
1) DNS-stability gate: wait_for_dns helper (new): queries expected host 5x with linear backoff; requires N consecutive successful answers. Pros: fewer flapping cases during bootstrap. Cons: adds time to install on slow DNS.
2) Probing via mTLS pre-warm: run a short TLS handshake to registry IP (if cached) before starting services. If handshake fails with name resolution issues, backoff and retry.
3) On-host resolv.conf patching (opt-in): temporarily point to 127.0.0.1 stub resolver we start during install to avoid customer DNS weirdness. This is invasive and gated behind a flag.
4) Truncate-detect and TCP-unblock detection: run DNS queries with EDNS0 and detect TC bit; warn in logs and prompt field eng to open TCP 53.

Observability & metrics we added: (quick list)
- install.dns.resolve_latency_ms (histogram) — measured at the helper step
- install.dns.resolve_consistency_count — number of consecutive identical answers
- install.playbook.step_delay_seconds — to monitor slowdowns introduced by gates
- healthcheck.fail_reason (tagged: dns|tcp|cert|timeout) — surfaced to Console as temporary chart for installs

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Acceptable install latency bump: product wants <= 30s extra on average for determinism; experiments currently add 10–20s. Can we tune thresholds? (ask: product/console team)
- Stub resolver option: safety review required before enabling by default. Legal/security flagged potential for changing resolv.conf on customer hosts — need ops signoff.
- Should we attempt automatic TCP/53 unblocking via a transient NAT traversal? Risky. Probably policy: surface to field eng and provide manual checklist.

Action items (owners):
- Ravi: consolidate the DNS helper into playbook core + submit PR with opt-in flag (due 2027-03-12).
- Liam: add the EDNS0 truncate detector and loggable hint in installer (due 2027-03-11).
- Gina: draft a short one-page pre-install checklist for appliances with older DNS stacks and share with field-eng (due 2027-03-10).
- Alex: add metrics dashboard tile to Console dev namespace for install.healthcheck.fail_reason (due 2027-03-14).
- Priya: create a CS escalation template to request DNS TTL/records verification from customer DNS teams (due 2027-03-13).

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- re-run PR-342 canary across three different cloud providers (GCP/OCI/AWS) to ensure resolver semantics differences handled.
- follow up with infra on whether iptables changes (for stub resolver approach) can be automatically reverted on failure.
- collect more logs of truncated DNS responses and attach examples to JIRA-PLAT-1198.

Meeting cadence & syncs this week:
- Wed 09:30 — quick hands-on with field eng (recorded) — walk-through of playbook change.
- Thu 16:00 — cross-team postmortem with customer success and field team for AURORA-21.
- Fri 11:00 — install playbook review: decide gating thresholds.

Appendix: quick reproducible check (to share with field)
1) On target host: dig +short @127.0.0.1 your.registry.example A
2) If no consistent answers: run tcpdump -n -s 0 -w dns-trace.pcap port 53 and reproduce a failing install attempt; attach pcap to ticket.
3) If EDNS truncation observed (TC=1), request TCP/53 allowed for the install window.

Final thought: these DNS edge cases are noisy but low-frequency; pragmatic, reversible playbook changes (backoff, flush, early-detect) seem to reduce pain materially without heavy customer changes. Keep playbook changes opt-in until we validate across clouds and appliances.

(End of notes)
